# ef-core — a migration generated by the tool, read as SQL before any database runs it

**Contract.** A generated migration, its idempotent script shown, applied only on an explicit yes to
the local database · never hand-writes a migration class or edits the model snapshot (the generated
`Up`/`Down` bodies may be edited, e.g. an explicit rename), never `database update` on a shared
database · prose in the chat language, SQL and tool output verbatim.

## When

Not for: query plans, indexes, deadlocks (`db-analyst`); a schema managed outside EF (Dapper-only
projects, a read cache): no context is added to get migrations; test setup (`dotnet-testing`).

House facts: rule `ef-migrations`. A repository's own data playbook wins over this skill.

## Decide

| Situation | Move |
| --- | --- |
| the model changed | change the model first, then generate; never write the class to match |
| several `DbContext`s | ask which; `--context` on every later command |
| migrations pending before yours | report the backlog, the user decides; never stack silently |
| `has-pending-model-changes` says none | stop: an empty migration is noise |
| the script drops, narrows or tightens | a decision for the user, even when they asked for it (`references/migrations.md` § What to look for) |
| a column or table goes away | expand, deploy, contract: two deployments |
| the migration is wrong, applied only on your machine | `migrations remove`, fix the model, regenerate |
| the migration is wrong, applied anywhere shared | a new corrective migration; never remove or edit it |
| "apply it too" said up front | skips the asking, never the showing |

## Do

```powershell
dotnet tool restore                                 # if dotnet-ef is pinned in a tool manifest
dotnet ef migrations list                           # what exists, which are applied
dotnet ef migrations has-pending-model-changes      # anything to migrate at all
dotnet ef dbcontext info                            # provider and connection really resolved, every time
dotnet ef migrations add <IntentInPascalCase>       # then read Up AND Down
dotnet ef migrations script --idempotent -o "$([IO.Path]::GetTempPath())review.sql"
```

Then **stop and show the SQL**: tables touched, destructive statements, whether `Down` inverts `Up`,
a backfill the migration lacks. Apply only on a yes, to the local database, named first. The full
procedure with its report: `references/migrations.md`.

## Traps

1. `Value cannot be null. (Parameter 'input')` → the design-time factory rewrites the connection from
   an unset variable → set `ConnectionStrings__<Ctx>` for the call; real fix: a null guard.
2. `Unable to create a DbContext` → no design-time factory and the startup project cannot build its
   configuration → add a factory, or point `--startup-project` at the real host.
3. A migration applied to the wrong database → `database update` used what the factory resolved
   (`DOTNET_ENVIRONMENT` changes it) → `dotnet ef dbcontext info` first.
4. A drop plus an add of a similar column → EF read a rename as drop-and-recreate → rewrite it as a
   rename so the data survives.
5. Two branches each added a migration → the snapshots conflict → `references/migrations.md` § Commit hygiene.
